title: A lost migration checkpoint wedges every later migration for good
body:
## Summary
The non-idempotent migrations (CREATE INDEX, ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN) re-run after a failed checkpoint and then fail every time, so no later migration ever runs again.

## Description
@forge/sql 4.0.9 MigrationRunner.run() (node_modules/@forge/sql/out/migration.js) runs `executeDDL(statement)` and only then INSERTs the name into __migrations; a failed INSERT throws MigrationCheckPointError with the DDL already applied. forge/src/adapters/forge-sql.mjs:50-52 enqueues every MIGRATIONS entry and calls run(). In forge/src/sql/migrations.mjs, v004/v005/v007/v010/v014/v029 are `CREATE INDEX` without IF NOT EXISTS (e.g. forge/src/sql/migrations.mjs:78) and v016-v022/v025/v026 are `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` (forge/src/sql/migrations.mjs:199). On the next run the unrecorded statement executes again, TiDB answers duplicate column/key name, run() throws MigrationExecutionError and stops before every later name. The file is append-only (forge/src/sql/migrations.mjs:4), so the shipped statements cannot simply gain IF NOT EXISTS. Then forge/src/index.js:47-56 withSchema retries the same failing run on every call that hits the missing column.

## Flow
- v016 ALTER succeeds; the INSERT INTO __migrations request fails (one HTTP POST each, forge-sql.mjs header)
- next migrate: v016 is not in __migrations, ALTER runs again, Duplicate column name, MigrationExecutionError
- v017..v031 never run; any query on verdicts.snooze_until is ER_BAD_FIELD_ERROR
- every resolver/tool call answers unavailable "storage is not ready" until someone edits __migrations by hand

## Expected impact
An installation that loses one checkpoint request stops working until someone fixes it by hand. The fix: in runMigrations, treat a MigrationExecutionError whose cause is errno 1060/1061 (duplicate column / key name) as already applied, record the name, and run the rest.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a transient checkpoint failure no longer bricks the schema.
Before: a re-run of an applied ALTER/CREATE INDEX fails forever (read from out/migration.js run()).
After: the duplicate-DDL error is recorded as applied and later migrations run.
Method: simulation - walked three cases (checkpoint lost on v016 ALTER; on v029 CREATE INDEX; on v031 CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, which is already safe); no TiDB reachable to probe.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: node_modules/@forge/sql/out/migration.js run(): `await this.sqlClient.executeDDL(migration.statement);` then `throw new errors_1.MigrationCheckPointError(...)` around INSERT_SCHEMA_VERSION_QUERY; forge/src/sql/migrations.mjs:78 `{ name: 'v004_proposals_status_ix', statement: 'CREATE INDEX ix_proposals_status ON proposals (project_key, status, last_push_at)' }`; forge/src/sql/migrations.mjs:199 `{ name: 'v016_proposals_snooze_until', statement: 'ALTER TABLE proposals ADD COLUMN snooze_until VARCHAR(10)' }`; forge/src/adapters/forge-sql.mjs:51-52 `for (const m of MIGRATIONS) migrationRunner.enqueue(m.name, m.statement); return migrationRunner.run();`
impact_why: One lost request leaves an installation permanently unavailable; recovery needs a manual SQL edit

title: Log the failing migration's name when storage is not ready
body:
## Summary
safe() logs only the error class name, so a wedged migration leaves just "storage not ready (MigrationExecutionError)" in the logs, with no migration name, no cause and no hint.

## Description
forge/src/index.js:83 logs `dowser: storage not ready (<e.name>)` for every non-consent error that escapes, and answers "try again in a minute" (forge/src/index.js:84). @forge/sql MigrationExecutionError and MigrationCheckPointError carry migrationName, migrationsYetToRun and cause (node_modules/@forge/sql/out/errors.d.ts), and ForgeSQLAPIError carries code and responseDetails.traceId. None of these contain user content, so logging them is safe under the "no body in errors" rule (forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:42-43).

## Flow
- a migration fails inside withSchema
- the log reads "storage not ready (MigrationExecutionError)"
- the operator cannot tell which migration, or whether it is transient, without redeploying with more logging

## Expected impact
Log one JSON line with name, code, migrationName, migrationsYetToRun.length and the traceId. Then the wedge in forge/src/sql/migrations.mjs is visible from `forge logs`.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - diagnosability of storage failures.
Before: error class name only (index.js:83).
After: the failing migration name, error code and trace id.
Method: simulation - walked MigrationExecutionError, ForgeSQLAPIError (ER_NO_SUCH_TABLE), and a plain Error; all fields are metadata.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/index.js:83 `console.error(`dowser: storage not ready (${String(/** @type {any} */ (e)?.name ?? typeof e)})`);`; node_modules/@forge/sql/out/errors.d.ts `export declare class MigrationExecutionError extends ForgeSQLError { readonly migrationName: string; readonly migrationsYetToRun: string[]; readonly cause?: Error`
impact_why: Turns a silent outage into a named one in forge logs

title: Schema retry marks an installation migrated before the migration succeeds
body:
## Summary
ensureSchema and withSchema add the installation to `migrated` before awaiting runMigrations, so one failed or in-flight migration disables the retry for the rest of the warm runtime.

## Description
forge/src/index.js:34-36 (ensureSchema) and forge/src/index.js:52-54 (withSchema) both do `migrated.add(inst); await runMigrations();`. If runMigrations throws (a transient Forge SQL 5xx), the set still holds the installation; every later call that hits the missing table sees `migrated.has(inst)` and rethrows (forge/src/index.js:34, :52), answering "storage is not ready" until the runtime recycles or the daily trigger runs. A second call that arrives while the first is still migrating also fails right away instead of waiting. The two functions are a pair holding the same rule twice.

## Flow
- call A hits ER_NO_SUCH_TABLE, adds inst, runMigrations rejects (HTTP 503)
- call B hits the same table: migrated.has(inst) is true, so it rethrows, safe() answers unavailable
- every call until the runtime dies or dowser-migrate-daily runs fails the same way

## Expected impact
Keep one per-installation promise (Map inst -> Promise), delete it on rejection, and have concurrent callers await it. That folds ensureSchema and withSchema into one helper.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failed in-request migration is retried on the next call; concurrent calls wait instead of failing.
Before: one rejection blocks retries for the runtime lifetime (forge/src/index.js:35, :53 add before await).
After: a rejection clears the entry; the next call migrates again.
Method: simulation - walked (1) transient failure then retry, (2) two concurrent calls, (3) success path unchanged; index.js imports @forge/api so no unit probe without module mocks.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/index.js:34-36 `if (migrated.has(inst) || !isSchemaBehind(e)) return false; migrated.add(inst); await runMigrations();`; forge/src/index.js:52-54 `if (migrated.has(inst) || !isSchemaBehind(e)) throw e; migrated.add(inst); await runMigrations();`
impact_why: A transient SQL failure during a minor-deploy migration makes the app unavailable for the runtime lifetime

title: One hidden or deleted issue key fails the whole status batch
body:
## Summary
The port promises that a key the user cannot see is simply absent, but issueStatuses sends `key in (...)` JQL, which Jira refuses outright when any listed key does not exist or is not visible.

## Description
forge/src/core/ports.mjs:49 says issueStatuses "answers only the keys Jira returned (a missing key is one the user cannot browse, or gone)", and forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:171-172 repeats it. The adapter posts a `key in (...)` JQL (forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:182) for chunks of 50. Jira JQL validation answers 400 ("An issue with key ... does not exist for field key") for an unknown or invisible key, and json() throws (forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:51). candidatesOf catches it and drops ALL statuses (forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:327), so every candidate shows "unknown". Deleted issues are a designed case (the dowser-issue-deleted trigger, forge/manifest.yml:273), and accepts may target projects other viewers cannot browse (atlassian.mjs:171), so this is the normal case, not an edge.

## Flow
- DW-1 accepted into SHOP-1, DW-2 into a private project HR-7
- a viewer without HR access opens Learning
- JQL key in (SHOP-1,HR-7) answers 400, so the whole chunk throws
- SHOP-1 shows "unknown" too, and the done flag is false for every candidate

## Expected impact
Use POST /rest/api/3/issue/bulkfetch (issueIdsOrKeys, fields [status]), which returns the visible issues and lists the rest under issueErrors. The other way is to pass the query with validation off. Either makes the port contract true.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - statuses survive one unreadable key.
Before: one bad key in a chunk of 50 blanks all 50 statuses (reflect.mjs:327 catch).
After: only the unreadable key is absent.
Method: simulation - walked a chunk with all-visible keys (unchanged), one deleted key, one invisible key; no Jira site reachable to probe, Jira behaviour from its JQL validation rules.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/core/ports.mjs:49 ` *  `issueStatuses` reads as the calling user and answers only the keys Jira returned (a missing key is one the user`; forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:182 `body: JSON.stringify({ jql: `key in (${chunk.join(',')})`, maxResults: chunk.length, fields: ['status'] }),`; forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:327 `try { status = await deps.jira.issueStatuses([...]) } catch (e) {` (logs warn, status stays {})
impact_why: The Learning tab loses every issue status as soon as one accepted issue is deleted or private to the viewer

title: Jira project picker silently stops at 1000 projects
body:
## Summary
listProjects stops paging at startAt 1000 and returns the partial list as if it were complete.

## Description
forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:150 `for (let startAt = 0; startAt < 1000;)` with nothing to say the list was cut. jira.projects (forge/src/core/app.mjs:244-250) hands it to the Settings/accept dialogs (forge/static/app/src/routes/inbox/dialogs.jsx:29), which cannot tell the difference. On a large site the project a team wants is just not offered.

## Flow
- a site with 1400 browsable projects
- Settings lists projects 1-1000 in API order
- the team's project is missing, and nothing says the list is partial

## Expected impact
Return a `truncated: true` flag (or take a search query: project/search accepts `query`) and show "type to search" when it is set.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - large sites can pick any project.
Before: a silent cut at 1000.
After: a flagged cut or a server-side search.
Method: simulation - walked 40, 1000 and 1400 projects.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:150 `for (let startAt = 0; startAt < 1000;) {`; forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:159 `if (page.isLast !== false || !(page.values ?? []).length) break;`
impact_why: Only enterprise sites hit it, but there the accept target cannot be chosen

title: Issue-property backfill failure skips the page-link backfill, mislabelled
body:
## Summary
migrate() runs both backfills in one try, so a failing issue-property backfill skips backfillPageLinks, and a failing page-link backfill is logged as an issue-property failure.

## Description
forge/src/index.js:184-191: backfillIssueProperties then backfillPageLinks inside one try; the catch logs "issue-property backfill failed" (forge/src/index.js:190). These are independent jobs (core/issue-property.mjs vs core/doc-drift.mjs).

## Flow
- Jira answers 5xx during backfillIssueProperties
- backfillPageLinks never runs that day, so byline/banner links stay missing for pre-v030 items
- or: page-link backfill throws, and the log blames the issue-property backfill

## Expected impact
Two try/catch blocks with their own labels, so each backfill runs and reports on its own.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - each backfill runs whatever the other does.
Before: one failure skips the other and mislabels the log.
After: independent runs, correct labels.
Method: simulation - walked both-succeed, first-fails, second-fails.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/index.js:184-190 `try { const b = await backfillIssueProperties(deps()); ... const l = await backfillPageLinks(deps()); ... } catch (e) { console.error(`dowser: issue-property backfill failed (...)`);`
impact_why: Daily backfills are independent; one should not cost the other a day

title: Atlassian adapter header misstates who reads issue statuses
body:
## Summary
The adapter's identity table says issue statuses are read AS APP, but the code, a test and the method comment all say AS USER. The endpoint list also leaves out four calls the file makes.

## Description
forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:14 "Issue statuses and display names: AS APP". issueStatuses uses asUser() (forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:179), its own comment says "Read AS THE USER" (forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:171), and forge/test/adapter-identity.test.mjs:19 asserts it. The REST list (forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:16-24) omits PUT /issue/{key}/properties/{key} (:166), POST /wiki/api/v2/footer-comments (:199), the Teamwork Graph query (:283) and the status use of POST /search/jql. This header is what a scope review reads.

## Flow
- a reviewer checks the identity table for a permissions audit
- reads statuses as app, so it looks like a cross-project leak risk the code already closed
- misses the v2 footer-comment write when matching scopes in manifest.yml:308-318

## Expected impact
Fix line 14 (statuses AS USER, names AS APP) and complete the endpoint list.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the header matches the code.
Before: line 14 contradicts :171/:179 and the test.
After: one consistent statement.
Method: simulation - re-read all three places.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:14 `//  - Issue statuses and display names: AS APP (read-only, for items the person already opened).`; forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:171 `// Read AS THE USER: the Learning tab must not show the status of an issue in a project the viewer cannot browse`; forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:179 `const res = await asUser().requestJira(route`/rest/api/3/search/jql`, {`
impact_why: The identity table is the security-relevant summary; it contradicts the code

title: A failing user-name batch is swallowed with no log line
body:
## Summary
users.names drops a failed batch silently, so a permanent failure (a revoked read:jira-user scope, a 403) shows raw account ids forever and leaves no trace in the logs.

## Description
forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:221 `} catch { /* omit this batch's names */ }`. Dropping the names is right (forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:210), but the failure is never counted or logged. Other soft failures in the core do log a warn line (forge/src/core/reflect.mjs:327-328).

## Flow
- Jira user/bulk answers 403 after a scope change
- every decider shows as an account id in inbox history
- forge logs show nothing

## Expected impact
Log one warn line per call naming the HTTP status and the batch count, never the ids.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - a degraded nicety becomes visible.
Before: no signal.
After: a warn line with the status.
Method: simulation - walked ok, a transient 5xx and a permanent 403.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/adapters/atlassian.mjs:219-221 `const page = await json(await asApp().requestJira(route`/rest/api/3/user/bulk?${q}`), 'Jira user bulk'); ... } catch { /* omit this batch's names */ }`
impact_why: Cheap signal for a silent degradation

title: Tool choice can come from a payload-supplied moduleKey
body:
## Summary
mcp() and rovo() accept payload.context.moduleKey as a candidate action key. When the runtime does not set the module key, the payload decides which handler runs, not the action the platform invoked.

## Description
forge/src/index.js:130 and forge/src/index.js:142 pass [runtimeModuleKey(), context?.moduleKey, payload?.context?.moduleKey] to actionName, which returns the first known name (forge/src/core/app.mjs actionName). The action's manifest verb (GET vs CREATE/UPDATE, forge/manifest.yml:42 vs :162) is what Rovo uses to decide whether to ask the person for confirmation. So a GET action whose payload names dowser_verdict_record could record a verdict without that prompt. Whether the platform lets a model put a context key into an action payload is not documented here. Access checks still run on the chosen handler (core/app.mjs TOOLS/ROVO), so this widens the verb, not the data reach.

## Flow
- getAppContext().moduleKey is undefined for the invocation (the fallback exists for that case, index.js:122-123)
- a dowser_inbox_list (GET) call arrives with payload.context.moduleKey = dowser_verdict_record
- the UPDATE handler runs without Rovo's write confirmation

## Expected impact
Drop the payload candidate, or accept it only when it maps to an action with the same manifest verb as the invoked one.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - the invoked action alone selects the handler verb.
Before: payload can steer to a write handler.
After: only platform-set keys or shape inference.
Method: simulation - walked runtime key set (no change), runtime key absent with payload key, neither; platform behaviour not probed.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/src/index.js:142 `const name = actionName('rovo', [runtimeModuleKey(), context?.moduleKey, /** @type {any} */ (payload)?.context?.moduleKey], payload);`; forge/src/core/app.mjs `for (const c of candidates) if (c && known.includes(c)) return c;`
impact_why: Only matters if the runtime key is absent; then a read action can run a write without confirmation
